items.title: Create and approve an incident response plan
items.result: Develop, approve, and maintain a written plan covering preparation, detection, containment, eradication, recovery, documentation, escalation, and post-incident review.

items.title: Define incident roles and contact paths
items.result: Assign incident owners, deputies, decision authorities, escalation routes, and internal and external contact paths, with regular review and availability checks.

items.title: Implement traceable incident detection and records
items.result: Implement monitoring, triage, severity assessment, evidence preservation, case tracking, approvals, and audit trails for security incidents from detection through closure.

items.title: Implement timely significant-incident reporting
items.result: Establish a documented workflow for assessing significance, approving notifications, tracking reporting deadlines, submitting updates, and retaining transmission records.

items.title: Establish security accountability and management oversight
items.result: Designate an information-security owner, document responsibilities, and require management approval and periodic oversight of security measures. Implement recurring cybersecurity training for management and retain attendance records.

items.title: Establish documented risk analysis
items.result: Create and approve a documented risk analysis covering IT systems, important data, and business processes. Record identified risks, impacts, likelihoods, owners, and treatment decisions.

items.title: Define risk analysis review triggers
items.result: Implement a review process requiring regular updates and reassessment after major changes or security incidents. Record review dates, triggers, findings, and approvals.

items.title: Identify critical operational dependencies
items.result: Document critical business processes, IT systems, important data, and providers, including owners, dependencies, service importance, and recovery priorities.

items.title: Maintain a current asset inventory
items.result: Establish and maintain an inventory of devices, software, cloud services, user accounts, and important data. Assign owners and define update and reconciliation responsibilities.

items.title: Establish supplier identification and security risk assessment
items.result: Create and maintain an inventory of important IT providers and suppliers, then assess and document their security risks using defined criteria.

items.title: Define security requirements for important provider contracts
items.result: Update contracts with important providers to specify IT security controls, incident notification, cooperation, and relevant assurance requirements.

items.title: Implement provider outage and exit planning
items.result: Establish documented procedures for provider outages and security problems, including escalation, communications, continuity measures, replacement, and orderly service exit.

items.title: Implement least-privilege access reviews
items.result: Define role-based access profiles, grant only documented business needs, and review permissions regularly with recorded approvals and removals.

items.title: Automate personnel access changes
items.result: Establish joiner, mover, and leaver workflows that promptly adjust or disable accounts after approved personnel changes, with completion tracking.

items.title: Deploy multi-factor authentication
items.result: Require multi-factor authentication for sensitive systems, administrator accounts, and remote access, and monitor enrollment and enforcement coverage.

items.title: Implement encryption for sensitive data and connections
items.result: Define encryption requirements for sensitive data and important connections, then deploy approved protections and verify coverage through documented testing.

items.title: Establish resilient secure communication channels
items.result: Provide secure communication channels for routine operations, emergencies, and outages, with documented fallback procedures and periodic failover testing.

items.title: Protect systems and rooms from physical hazards
items.result: Implement access controls and environmental safeguards for important systems and rooms, covering unauthorized entry, power loss, fire, water, and other identified hazards.

items.title: Integrate security into system lifecycles
items.result: Define security requirements for acquisition, development, and change, with documented reviews and approval gates throughout each system lifecycle.

items.title: Implement controlled patch management
items.result: Establish an inventory-based patch process that prioritizes, tests, deploys, tracks, and documents security updates within defined timeframes.

items.title: Implement vulnerability management
items.result: Establish a controlled process to identify, assess, prioritize, remediate, track, and appropriately disclose vulnerabilities across the system lifecycle.

items.title: Implement backup and recovery controls
items.result: Establish regular backups for important data and systems, protect them from alteration or deletion, and store them separately. Define recovery responsibilities and objectives, then test restoration regularly and document results.

items.title: Establish regular security effectiveness reviews
items.result: Define a recurring review schedule, assess implemented security measures against approved criteria, document findings, and assign accountable owners for deficiencies.

items.title: Implement accountable remediation tracking
items.result: Create a remediation register capturing each deficiency, accountable owner, target deadline, status, and evidence demonstrating completed implementation.

items.title: Implement recurring training and binding cyber-hygiene rules
items.result: Create recurring, role-appropriate training covering phishing, passwords, data protection, and secure working. Publish binding, accessible rules for passwords, updates, email, mobile devices, and remote work, with completion tracking and periodic review.

automaticChecks.name: NIS2-GOV-01 atomic Gap contract
automaticChecks.expected: one or more one-line atomic gaps of at most 20 words

actual.statement: No person or team is clearly designated as responsible for IT security.
Management does not approve and oversee important IT security measures.
Management does not regularly attend training on cyber risks and IT security.

automaticChecks.name: NIS2-RISK-02 atomic Gap contract
automaticChecks.expected: one or more one-line atomic gaps of at most 20 words

actual.statement: A written risk analysis covering IT systems, data, and important business processes is not in place.
Regular updates to the risk analysis after major changes or security incidents are not implemented.
Critical business processes, IT systems, data, and providers are not identified.
An up-to-date inventory of devices, software, cloud services, user accounts, and important data is not maintained.

automaticChecks.name: NIS2-IAM-03 atomic Gap contract
automaticChecks.expected: one or more one-line atomic gaps of at most 20 words

actual.statement: Employees do not receive only necessary access rights, and regular access reviews are not implemented.
Accounts are not promptly adjusted or disabled when personnel change roles or leave.
Multi-factor authentication is not implemented for sensitive, administrative, and remote access.

automaticChecks.name: NIS2-IR-04 atomic Gap contract
automaticChecks.expected: one or more one-line atomic gaps of at most 20 words

actual.statement: No written incident-response plan is implemented.
Roles, deputies, and incident contact paths are not defined.
Traceable incident detection, assessment, and documentation are not implemented.
Timely significant-incident reporting procedures are not implemented.

automaticChecks.name: NIS2-BC-05 atomic Gap contract
automaticChecks.expected: one or more one-line atomic gaps of at most 20 words

actual.statement: Regular backups of important data and systems are not implemented.
Backups are not protected from modification or deletion or stored separately from normal systems.
Regular testing of data and system restoration from backups is not implemented.
An emergency and recovery plan defining processes, responsibilities, and recovery objectives is not implemented.

automaticChecks.name: NIS2-SC-06 atomic Gap contract
automaticChecks.expected: one or more one-line atomic gaps of at most 20 words

actual.statement: Important IT providers and suppliers are not consistently identified and assessed for security risk.
Contracts with important providers do not contain clear requirements for IT security and security incidents.
No process exists for outages, security problems, or replacing an important provider.

automaticChecks.name: NIS2-VM-07 atomic Gap contract
automaticChecks.expected: one or more one-line atomic gaps of at most 20 words

actual.statement: Security requirements are not integrated into IT system acquisition, development, and change.
A controlled process for applying security updates and patches promptly is not implemented.
A controlled process for identifying, assessing, remediating, and disclosing vulnerabilities is not implemented.

automaticChecks.name: NIS2-ASSURE-08 atomic Gap contract
automaticChecks.expected: one or more one-line atomic gaps of at most 20 words

actual.statement: Regular reviews of implemented security measure effectiveness are not in place.
Tracking identified gaps with owners, deadlines, and implementation evidence is not in place.

automaticChecks.name: NIS2-AWARE-09 atomic Gap contract
automaticChecks.expected: one or more one-line atomic gaps of at most 20 words

actual.statement: Regular, understandable training on phishing, passwords, data protection, and secure working is not implemented.
Binding basic rules for secure working, including passwords, updates, email, mobile devices, and remote work, are not implemented.

automaticChecks.name: NIS2-PROTECT-10 atomic Gap contract
automaticChecks.expected: one or more one-line atomic gaps of at most 20 words

actual.statement: Sensitive data and important connections are not encrypted appropriately.
Secure communication channels are not available for normal operations, emergencies, or failures of usual systems.
Important IT systems and rooms lack protection against unauthorized access and physical or environmental hazards.

automaticChecks.name: Independent Action Plan prompt and response contract

actions.title: Create and approve an incident response plan
actions.result: Develop, approve, and maintain a written plan covering preparation, detection, containment, eradication, recovery, documentation, escalation, and post-incident review.

actions.title: Define incident roles and contact paths
actions.result: Assign incident owners, deputies, decision authorities, escalation routes, and internal and external contact paths, with regular review and availability checks.

actions.title: Implement traceable incident detection and records
actions.result: Implement monitoring, triage, severity assessment, evidence preservation, case tracking, approvals, and audit trails for security incidents from detection through closure.

actions.title: Implement timely significant-incident reporting
actions.result: Establish a documented workflow for assessing significance, approving notifications, tracking reporting deadlines, submitting updates, and retaining transmission records.

automaticChecks.name: Action coverage
automaticChecks.expected: every gap covered and every action linked
